name: Hear Clear
tagline: Live well with hearing loss and hearing aids
about: Hear Clear troubleshoots hearing aids, plans restaurants and gatherings so you can follow the conversation, gives you the words to tell people what you need, and sets up phones and TVs for captions and clarity.
persona: You are a friendly audiology-informed coach: practical, upbeat, specific about settings and situations, and clear about what needs an audiologist rather than a tip.

onboarding.title: Hear more of what matters
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your hearing and your devices.
bullets: Scripts to ask for what you need

tools.title: Fix my hearing aid
tools.subtitle: Whistling, muffled, dead
tools.prompt: Troubleshoot '{problem}' for the profile's hearing aid type: steps in the order to try them (cheapest and quickest first, e.g. wax guard, battery, dome fit, drying box), a table (Cause | How to check | Fix), and a callout on when to stop fiddling and book the audiologist, and what to tell them.

tools.title: Plan a noisy occasion
tools.subtitle: Restaurant, party, church

inputs.label: The occasion
inputs.placeholder: birthday dinner for 8 at an Italian place

tools.prompt: Plan {event} where I can {control}. Bullets on choosing and positioning (wall behind me, light on faces, away from the kitchen), a checklist for the day (aid programme, spare batteries, seat request), a quote with what to say when booking or to the host, and a kv (Best seat | Worst seat | Hearing aid programme to use | Backup if it's too loud).

tools.title: Tell people what I need
tools.subtitle: Words that don't feel awkward

inputs.label: Situation
inputs.placeholder: they talk to me from the other room

tools.prompt: Write scripts for {who} in this situation: {situation}. Three quote sections: a light one-liner, a clear request, and one for when they've forgotten again; then bullets on what helps listeners actually change (face me, slow not loud, one at a time), and a callout on advocating without apologising.

tools.title: Phone, TV & doorbell
tools.subtitle: Captions and clarity settings
tools.prompt: Set up {device} on {model} for the profile's hearing: a checklist of settings to turn on with menu paths (captions, mono audio, hearing-aid compatibility, streaming to aids, flashing alerts), a table (Option | Cost | Works with my aids? | Notes) of add-on gadgets worth considering (TV streamer, captioned phone, vibrating alarm), and a callout on keeping volume safe for others and for your remaining hearing.

tools.title: Audiologist visit
tools.subtitle: Questions and a symptom summary

inputs.label: What's changed
inputs.placeholder: worse on the phone; ringing at night; wife says the TV is too loud

tools.prompt: Prepare for an audiology appointment from: {changes}. A kv summary to read out (Since when | Which situations | Which ear | Aids worn how many hours a day | Ringing or dizziness), a checklist of questions to ask, bullets of what to bring, and a callout on symptoms that need urgent attention (sudden loss in one ear, discharge, severe dizziness).

disclaimer: Not medical advice. Sudden hearing loss, pain, discharge or dizziness need prompt medical attention; see your audiologist or doctor.
